newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Marks & Spencer profits disappoint.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Marks & Spencer profits disappoint.

text.p: Britain's biggest clothing retailer Marks & Spencer on Tuesday said a return of consumer confidence helped boost first half profits by 11.6 percent, but its shares dived as the results were below expectations.
Higher costs associated with hiring 2,000 extra staff in Britain over the current year meant profits came in 20 to 30 million pounds lower than expected, retail analysts said.
Pretax profits in the half year to September 28 rose to 430.1 million pounds ($704 million) from 385.4 million. But the market had expected profits of about 450 million pounds.
Sales rose nine percent to 3.53 billion pounds. The dividend was up 10 percent to 3.3 pence.
Marks' shares fell 16.5 pence to 492.5 pence.
Retail analysts said the investment in staff would pay dividends in the long run, but disappointment at the smaller than expected profit increase would prompt downgrades in full year forecasts.
"We are reducing to 1,120 million pounds from 1,160 million pounds for the 1996/97 financial year," said one analyst who asked not to be identified.
The group, which also has stores in North America, continental Europe and Asia, said the additional staff would increase costs, but were essential for customer service.
Chairman Sir Richard Greenbury said, "Although this will inevitably increase our cost base, it is essential that we invest in appropriate levels of customer service."
Greenbury said in a statement that consumer confidence seemed to be returning in Britain, where sales were up by 8.4 percent to 221 million pounds.
"We have increased our market share in clothing, and have held our position in foods. We have maintained our margins across the business," he said.
Home furnishings benefited from the upturn in the British housing market, with sales up 27 percent. In foods, sales rose 6.6 percent to 1.23 billion pounds.

Overseas sales, including franchises, rose 12 percent to 591 million pounds, while profits were up 36 percent to 17 million pounds. Initial sales at the group's first store in Germany, which opened in Cologne at the beginning of October, were well above estimate, Greenbury said.
Brooks Brothers, with stores in Japan as well as the United States, returned to a profit of 1.1 million pounds after a loss of 2.5 million last time.
In Europe, profits were 11 million pounds, up 42 percent. Greenbury said Marks would double its presence in Spain in the next two years and further strengthen its position in France.

Sales to Marks' franchise stores around the world rose by 24 percent. It opened new stores in Cyprus, Indonesia, Israel, Portugal, Tenerife and Thailand in the first half. And since the end of the half year Marks has opened in the Czech Republic, signed an agreement for South Korea and is looking for franchise partners in the Gulf and Australia.
Financial services produced a 25 percent increase in profits to 33 million pounds. ($1=.6107 Pound)
